title: Control Plane Bootstrap, TF Modules & Rotation Checklist (WIP)
content:
Context and goal:

This doc is a compact, operational runbook for first-booting a private control plane into a customer VPC or on-prem environment using our Terraform modules, plus the step sequences for scaling and node/secret rotations with minimal disruption. It's intentionally prescriptive — follow checklists in order. This is a working draft: add missing edge-cases from recent installs.

High-level assumptions (read first):
- Ops user has VPN / bastion access + MFA to customer network.
- KMS/HSM credentials already negotiated via onboarding (see linked CONFLUENCE page).
- Customer provides an RDS/Postgres endpoint or we deploy a managed DB in their VPC per contract.
- Terraform state stored in customer S3-compatible bucket or our object storage with remote state locking (Dynamo/Consul) configured.
- Kubernetes cluster (EKS/GKE/Onprem K8s) is reachable from control plane subnets.

Preflight checklist (must pass before terraform apply):
- [ ] Confirm CIDR ranges, reserved IPs, and NAT/GW placement.
- [ ] Validate DNS delegation for control-plane.* hostnames and wildcard cert plans.
- [ ] IAM role trust established for infra automation account (ARNs).
- [ ] Customer firewall rules allow control-plane -> model-serving ingress on ports 443 and 8443 and metrics port 9100.
- [ ] Remote state bucket exists and locking tested (terraform init + plan dry-run).
- [ ] KMS key ARN available and kms:Decrypt policy attached to infra role.

Minimal bootstrap flow (fast path):
1) Checkout infra repo, branch new-customer/<short-name>-bootstrap
2) Populate terraform.tfvars with site-specific inputs. Key fields (examples):
   - customer_name = "acme-inc"
   - environment = "prod"
   - region = "us-east-2"
   - cp_subnet_ids = ["subnet-xxx", "subnet-yyy"]
   - postgres_endpoint = "postgres.acme.internal:5432"
   - kms_key_arn = "arn:aws:kms:us-east-2:123456:key/abcd"
   - object_store_bucket = "acme-rw-state"

3) terraform init -backend-config=...  (validate remote state access)
4) terraform plan -var-file=terraform.tfvars -out=tfplan
   - Look for diffs in security groups and IAM. If state drift with existing infra, stop and reconcile.
5) terraform apply tfplan

What the modules create (short):
- networking.module: VPC peering routes, subnets, NAT/GW, control-plane LB(s)
- kms.module: keys + alias binding (optionally no-op for customer-managed KMS)
- rds.module or db-connector.module: optional DB endpoint wiring
- controlplane.module: ASG/Managed instance groups for CP API servers, autoscaling config, LB + healthchecks
- secrets.module: rotates secrets into KMS+vault shim and populate initial vault entries

Post-apply quick sanity (30 minutes):
- [ ] LB DNS resolves and returns TLS cert
- [ ] /healthz on control plane returns 200 (hit through LB)
- [ ] Vault has required keys, check vault kv get cp/config
- [ ] Control plane connects to Postgres (check logs for successful DB connection)
- [ ] Tracing/metrics pipeline (Prometheus remote write) shows metrics from new hosts

Terraform module notes & gotchas (cribbed from installs):
- network.module: avoid implicit route overlap — module now requires explicit reserved_cidrs list. If customer VPC is shared, set shared_vpc = true to prevent deletions.
- secrets.module: version 0.3 introduced mandatory kms_key_arn. Older installs used local file encryption — migrate via secrets:migrate helper script.
- controlplane.module: default instance type is c6i.large; for onprem set instance_type = "baremetal" and use node_selector logic (see module docstring).
- state locking: if using self-hosted Consul, set consul_acl_token in backend config; loss here caused a failed concurrent apply in two installs.

Scaling guidance (predictable traffic growth):
- Baseline: 4 CP replicas for small customers (2 AZs), 8 replicas recommended for predictable throughput at 1k req/s.
- Autoscaling: controlplane.module exposes target_cpu_percent and target_rps thresholds. For stable latency keep CPU < 65% and p99 request latency < 200ms.
- Warm-up: when scaling up, pre-warm KV cache by replaying warmup script: scripts/warm_kv_cache.sh --target-url https://controlplane/api/warm/ --load 50rps for 5 minutes.
- Horizontal vs vertical: prefer horizontal for redundancy; for tiny clusters adjust instance_type to medium-sized with larger CPU/memory if horizontal scaling infeasible.

Planned upgrade & rotation sequence (zero-downtime pattern):
Goal: upgrade control plane binary + tf module changes, roll secrets/KMS keys and TLS certs with minimal disruption.
Order of operations (recommended):
A) Pre-upgrade checks (run 1-2 hours before):
   - [ ] Full backup of DB (pg_dump snapshot) + exported schema version
   - [ ] Export Vault keys and ensure seal/unseal procedures documented for site
   - [ ] Review release notes for binary; confirm no migration steps that require quiescing traffic
   - [ ] Increase observability retention window for 24 hours (capture pre/post performance)

B) Terraform plan for infra changes only (no CP image):
   - Run terraform plan and verify only expected infra diffs (SGs, new tags).
   - Apply infra changes first. If any subnet/route changes, schedule a separate maintenance window.

C) Rolling control plane upgrade (safe rolling restart):
   - Put canary: shift 5-10% of traffic to canary CP by updating LB weights (use traffic-shift script: tools/traffic-shift --from old --to canary --percent 10)
   - Deploy new binary to one canary replica (use deploy/rollout script). Wait 10m, run smoke suite:
       * smoke/auth, smoke/api-versions, smoke/kv-readwrite, smoke/streaming
       * check p99 and error rate (error rate < 0.5% to proceed)
   - If canary looks good, sequentially cordon+drain one old node, replace with new image, uncordon. Repeat for rest. Keep at least N-1 nodes available.

D) Secret/KMS rotation (after binary upgrade verified):
   - Add new KMS key in terraform (kms.module). Do NOT remove old key yet.
   - Re-encrypt secrets: run scripts/rekey-vault --new-kms-arn=... which writes new ciphertext blobs but keeps old copies.
   - Validate new secrets by forcing one CP replica to read new ciphertext (set env VAR FORCE_SECRET_VERSION=v2)
   - Gradual cutover: update secret metadata to point at v2, then in next maintenance cycle remove v1 after 7 days.

E) TLS cert rotation (if ACM/Let's Encrypt managed):
   - Provision new cert and attach to LB. Test a subset of hostnames via canary domain alias.
   - After 24h of stability, update DNS canonical records to new cert alias and retire old cert after TTL.

Rollbacks & emergency steps (cheat-sheet):
- If DB migration error: immediate rollback via DB restore (pg_restore) and revert CP to previous image tag.
- If p99 spikes > 2x baseline after a node rotation: pause rollout, re-add previous node, reduce concurrency, and open P0 incident.
- If Vault becomes unavailable during key rotate: run vault operator unseal steps and point CP to old key via env override VAULT_KEY_OVERRIDE=old; open incident and escalate to SRE.

Smoke tests and observability playbook (post-change):
- Run full smoke suite (scripts/smoke-runner --suite full) and capture traces.
- Dashboards to check: CP-Latency-overview, KV-errors, DB-conn-errors, Prometheus node exporter CPU/Memory
- Set temporary alert thresholds (e.g., p99 > 400ms OR error-rate > 1%) to be more sensitive for 6 hours after deploy

Operations checklist for node rotations (detailed):
1) Identify target node(s) via kubectl get nodes -l cp-role=primary
2) kubectl cordon <node>
3) kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --timeout=10m
4) Wait for workloads to be scheduled elsewhere and confirm LB health 200s from health checks
5) Run post-drain smoke on another replica to validate state
6) Update infra (if replacing instance) or patch OS/kernel and reboot
7) Rejoin: kubectl uncordon <node>
8) Monitor metrics for 15-30 minutes

Troubleshooting snippets (copy for SSH bastion):
- Check CP logs: journalctl -u redwood-controlplane -f --since "10m"
- Test DB connectivity: psql postgresql://user@postgres:5432/cpdb -c "select 1"
- Vault status: vault status -format=json | jq .
- Verify KMS decrypt locally: aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://secret.bin --key-id arn:aws:kms:... --query Plaintext --output text | base64 --decode

- Add preflight network probe tool to assert cross-AZ latency < 30ms (work in progress)
- Document bare-metal instance_type mapping and constraints for onprem installs
